questions.q: A cantilever beam of length L carries a point load W at the free end. What is the maximum bending moment?
questions.fact: VERDICT: The maximum bending moment occurs at the fixed support and equals WL (negative sign indicates hogging). WHY: Bending moment is the product of load and perpendicular distance from the point of interest to the load. TRAPS: Students often forget the negative sign or calculate it at the free end where it is zero. HOOK: Imagine holding a broomstick by one end; the twist you feel at your hand is maximum there.
questions.hint: Remember the sign convention: sagging is positive, hogging (cantilever fixed end) is negative.

questions.q: In a simple pendulum, if the length of the string is increased by 21%, what is the percentage increase in its time period?
questions.fact: VERDICT: The time period increases by 10%. WHY: Time period T is proportional to the square root of length L (T ∝ √L). If L becomes 1.21L, then T becomes √1.21 = 1.1 times original, which is a 10% increase. TRAPS: Candidates often assume linear proportionality and answer 21%. HOOK: Think of swinging on a playground swing; the longer the chains, the slower the swing.
questions.hint: Use the square root shortcut: √(1 + x/100) ≈ 1 + x/200 for small x.

questions.q: A steam engine operates between source temperature 500K and sink temperature 300K. What is the maximum theoretical efficiency?
questions.fact: VERDICT: The maximum efficiency is 40%. WHY: This is governed by Carnot efficiency formula η = 1 - (T_sink / T_source) = 1 - (300/500) = 0.4. TRAPS: Students might use Celsius temperatures directly without converting to Kelvin, leading to wrong results. HOOK: No real engine can beat this limit; it's the cosmic speed limit for heat engines.
questions.hint: Always convert temperatures to Kelvin before applying Carnot formula.

questions.q: For a fluid flowing through a pipe of constant diameter with no friction, which statement is true regarding pressure and velocity?
questions.fact: VERDICT: Pressure decreases as velocity increases. WHY: Bernoulli's principle states that in an inviscid flow, total energy per unit volume is constant; thus, kinetic energy increase (velocity) must come at the expense of pressure energy. TRAPS: Candidates confuse this with pipe diameter changes where area reduction causes velocity increase and pressure drop simultaneously. HOOK: Think of water spraying from a garden hose when you pinch it—the faster jet means lower pressure inside.
questions.hint: High speed = Low pressure; High pressure = Low speed (in horizontal flow).

questions.q: In machine design, what is the primary purpose of providing clearance between mating parts?
questions.a: To allow for assembly and thermal expansion
questions.fact: VERDICT: Clearance allows assembly and accommodates thermal growth. WHY: Without clearance, parts would jam during manufacturing tolerances or expand when heated, causing seizure. TRAPS: Some think clearance is only for lubrication; while it helps, its primary geometric purpose is fit and expansion allowance. HOOK: Imagine trying to slide a tight ring over a finger without any gap—you'd get stuck immediately.
questions.hint: Clearance prevents interference fits from becoming locked due to heat or manufacturing errors.

questions.q: Which of the following materials is typically used for making cutting tools in metal machining?
questions.fact: VERDICT: High Speed Steel is commonly used. WHY: HSS retains hardness at high temperatures generated during cutting, unlike plain carbon steels. TRAPS: Students might choose cast iron (too brittle) or aluminum (too soft). HOOK: Think of a chef's knife—it must stay sharp even after chopping hot vegetables; HSS does the same for metal.
questions.hint: Look for materials that maintain hardness under heat (red-hardness).

questions.q: In an internal combustion engine, what happens to the air-fuel mixture during the suction stroke?
questions.a: It is drawn into the cylinder at atmospheric pressure
questions.fact: VERDICT: The piston moves down, creating low pressure that draws in the mixture. WHY: The intake valve opens, and the expanding volume reduces pressure below atmospheric, causing flow. TRAPS: Candidates might think compression happens here; compression occurs in the compression stroke. HOOK: Like sucking water through a straw, lowering pressure at one end pulls fluid in.
questions.hint: Suction = Intake; Compression = Squeezing; Power = Firing; Exhaust = Blowing out.

questions.q: What is the main function of a flywheel in an engine?
questions.a: To store kinetic energy and smooth out speed fluctuations
questions.fact: VERDICT: It stores kinetic energy to smooth torque variations. WHY: During power strokes, it absorbs excess energy; during non-power strokes, it releases stored energy to maintain constant crankshaft speed. TRAPS: Some confuse it with a governor (which controls speed) or clutch (which connects/disconnects). HOOK: Think of a spinning top—it resists falling over and keeps moving smoothly even when you stop pushing it.
questions.hint: Flywheel = Energy Bank; Governor = Speed Controller.

questions.q: In heat transfer, if the temperature difference between two surfaces is doubled while all other factors remain constant, how does the rate of heat conduction change?
questions.fact: VERDICT: The rate of heat conduction doubles. WHY: Fourier's law states q = kA(ΔT)/L; heat flow is directly proportional to temperature difference ΔT. TRAPS: Students might confuse this with radiation (which goes as T⁴) or convection (complex). HOOK: Imagine walking down a hill—twice the slope means twice the speed downhill.
questions.hint: Conduction is linear with temperature difference; Radiation is exponential.

questions.q: Which type of joint is most suitable for connecting two plates when welding is not feasible?
questions.fact: VERDICT: Riveted joints are used when welding isn't possible. WHY: Rivets mechanically lock plates together without requiring heat or filler metals, making them ideal for dissimilar materials or field repairs. TRAPS: Candidates might suggest bolted joints (which require holes and bolts) but rivets are specifically for permanent mechanical fastening without welding. HOOK: Think of old bridges—they used rivets because they could be hammered in place without electricity.
questions.hint: Rivets = Permanent mechanical lock; Bolts = Removable connection.
